evidence.velocity_vs_rigour: Thrive in a fast-moving environment where the data landscape is constantly evolving as the product grows
evidence.velocity_vs_rigour_explanation: Fast-growth startup framing ('rocket ship', 'fast-moving') is balanced by explicit rigour language ('testing coverage', 'well-tested analytics layers', 'clean, documented, tested'), giving roughly equal weight to both.
evidence.domain_risk: give the business a clear picture of clinical outcomes, practice performance, customer health, and growth metrics
evidence.domain_risk_explanation: Errors affect internal business decisions and clinical-outcome reporting for a vet-tech SaaS but there is no regulatory, financial-reporting, or compliance framing anywhere in the JD.
evidence.collaboration_width: Product; Engineering; Commercial teams; wider Data team
evidence.data_team_maturity: Partner closely with the wider Data team to ensure analytics models sit on top of solid, well-engineered pipelines
evidence.data_team_maturity_explanation: A distinct Data team already exists with engineered pipelines for analytics to sit on top of, but the company is only 50 people and still defining modelling standards, placing it mid-maturity.
evidence.jd_authorship: Own the analytics layer of our data platform; writing, structuring, and maintaining the SQL models that power dashboards, product metrics, and business intelligence
evidence.jd_authorship_explanation: Responsibilities name specific technical deliverables (SQL models, naming conventions, documentation standards, testing coverage) with precise application context, reading like it was written by a hiring manager who does the work.
evidence.stakeholder_orientation: give the business a clear picture of clinical outcomes, practice performance, customer health, and growth metrics
evidence.stakeholder_orientation_explanation: Responsibilities span Product, Engineering, and Commercial teams with roughly equal emphasis, and the data team itself is a named partner, so no single audience dominates.
evidence.autonomy_level: Own the analytics layer of our data platform
evidence.autonomy_level_explanation: The role owns and defines modelling standards ('Define and enforce data modelling best practices') but also executes stakeholder requests directly ('translate that into clean SQL, and deliver answers'), mixing strategic ownership with execution.
evidence.ai_role_explanation: Company is described as 'AI-native' and 'AI-driven care guidance' but no AI skill is expected of the analytics engineer candidate anywhere in responsibilities or requirements.
evidence.testing_framing: Define and enforce data modelling best practices, including naming conventions, documentation standards, and testing coverage
evidence.testing_framing_explanation: Testing coverage is listed as something the candidate defines and enforces directly, an ownership verb in the responsibilities section.
evidence.loss_aversion_framing: Take ownership of data quality as a first principle, if something looks wrong, you investigate and fix it, you don't just flag it
evidence.loss_aversion_framing_explanation: Data quality and trust language recurs ('clean, reliable, well-documented', 'trusted across the business') but there is no regulatory or compliance register, keeping it at moderate rather than high.
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix: Own the analytics layer of our data platform; writing, structuring, and maintaining the SQL models
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix_explanation: The role both builds new analytics structure ('Own the analytics layer') and maintains/improves an existing data team's pipelines, a mix of greenfield and fix/scale work.
evidence.work_arrangement: Are excited to work in-person from our Paddington, London HQ
evidence.loss_aversion: Take ownership of data quality as a first principle, if something looks wrong, you investigate and fix it, you don't just flag it — reflects a fear of undetected data errors rather than regulatory exposure.

Transform raw data from our platform into clean, reliable, well-documented datasets that Product, Engineering, and Commercial teams can actually use
Build and maintain reports that give the business a clear picture of clinical outcomes, practice performance, customer health, and growth metrics
Define and enforce data modelling best practices, including naming conventions, documentation standards, and testing coverage
Partner closely with the wider Data team to ensure analytics models sit on top of solid, well-engineered pipelines
Work directly with stakeholders across the business to understand what they need to know, translate that into clean SQL, and deliver answers that drive decisions
